rows.scope: Apply mathematics to practical problems in daily life, society and workplaces.
Use a problem-solving cycle: analyze, plan, solve, justify and evaluate conclusions and their reasonableness.
Select appropriate tools (objects, manipulatives, pencil-and-paper and technology) and techniques (mental arithmetic, estimates, number sense).
Communicate mathematical ideas and reasoning using symbolic, diagrammatic, graphical and verbal representations.
Construct and use representations to organize, record and communicate mathematical ideas.
Identify and analyze mathematical relationships to connect and communicate ideas.
Explain and justify mathematical arguments using precise mathematical language in written or spoken form.
Represent outcomes of simple and compound events with lists and tree diagrams.
Choose and use simulations for simple and compound events with or without technology.
Use experimental results to predict and solve simple and compound probability questions.
Use theoretical probability to predict and solve simple and compound-event questions.
Calculate event and complement probabilities and explain their relationship.
Use qualitative and quantitative predictions and comparisons from simple probability experiments.
Determine experimental and theoretical probabilities for simple and compound events from data and sample spaces.
Display solutions of one-variable, two-step inequalities on number lines.
Model and solve inequalities in one variable requiring two steps.
Translate situations into one-variable equations or inequalities with variables on both sides and rational coefficients/constants.
Write a corresponding real-world situation for a one-variable equation or inequality with variables on both sides and rational terms.
Model and solve equations with one variable appearing on both sides, using rational coefficients/constants in mathematical and applied problems.
Calculate constant of proportionality k=y/x from mathematical and real-world relationships.
Distinguish proportional and nonproportional relationships in tables, graphs and equations, including y=kx and y=mx+b with b≠0.
Represent both proportional and nonproportional linear relationships verbally, in tables, graphs and equations reducible to y=mx+b.
Use models to approximate circumference and circle-area formulas, then connect them to exact formulas.
Derive lateral and total surface areas from nets of rectangular and triangular prisms and pyramids.
Explain cylinder volume V=Bh as base area multiplied by height.
Model the volume relationship between rectangular prisms and pyramids with congruent bases and heights.
Explain verbally and symbolically the volume relationship for triangular prisms and pyramids with congruent bases and heights.
Model the volume relationship between cylinders and cones with congruent bases and heights.
Use manipulatives, models or diagrams to explain the Pythagorean theorem.
Give informal arguments for triangle interior/exterior angle facts, parallel-line transversal angles and AA triangle-similarity criterion.
Compute circumference and area of circles.
Compute areas of composite figures assembled from listed polygon types plus semicircles and quarter circles.
material_bounds: rectangles, squares, parallelograms, trapezoids, triangles, semicircles, quarter circles

rows.scope: Connect prior surface-area models to lateral/total surface-area formulas for rectangular/triangular prisms and cylinders.
Solve volume problems for rectangular and triangular pyramids.
Solve volume problems for cylinders, cones and spheres.
Apply the Pythagorean theorem and its converse in problem solving.
Calculate coordinate-plane distance between two points using the Pythagorean theorem.
Generalize orientation and congruence properties of rotations, reflections, translations and dilations of plane figures.
Distinguish transformations that preserve congruence from those that do not.
Describe coordinate-plane translations, reflections over x- or y-axis, and rotations by 90°, 180°, 270° or 360° algebraically.
Model how dilation changes length measures and area of two-dimensional figures.
